notes.meaning: A person who welcomes correction shows a genuine desire to learn and grow wise. Someone who hates being corrected behaves like an unthinking animal that kicks against guidance. Accepting discipline helps us avoid repeating foolish mistakes.

The Lord looks with favor on people who act with kindness and honest goodwill toward others. But He condemns anyone who quietly plots evil schemes. God evaluates our hearts and holds deceitful planners accountable.

differ.view: Methodists emphasize that God's grace changes the heart first so a person can become good, and continuing in obedience increases that goodness and God's favor.

notes.meaning: No one can build a secure life by doing what is wrong, because wicked gains have no firm foundation. Righteous people, however, are deeply rooted in God like a strong tree that cannot be knocked down. True stability comes only from living in God's ways.

A capable, godly wife brings honor, joy, and strength to her husband, serving as a crown of dignity in his life. But a wife whose shameful conduct ruins her household slowly drains his spirit, like a rotting disease in his bones. A healthy home depends greatly on character and mutual respect.

Godly people aim for what is fair and right even in their secret thoughts. In contrast, the inner plans and advice of the wicked are aimed at cheating others. God sees our thoughts and holds our hidden intentions to His standard.

The schemes and words of wicked people are meant to harm or destroy others, often using lies and false accusations. But upright people use their voices to speak up and rescue those in danger. A timely, honest word can save an innocent person's life.

Wicked people may seem powerful for a moment, but when sudden trouble strikes, they fall and vanish. The families and homes of the righteous, however, endure because God protects them. God gives lasting security to those who walk uprightly.

People are truly respected when they show wise judgment and moral goodness in daily life. But anyone with a twisted, crooked mind earns only contempt from others. Real honor comes from walking in truth rather than pursuing clever schemes.

It is far better to live modestly and have enough food and help than to put on grand airs while starving at home. Pretending to be rich and important brings only empty pride and hidden misery. Quiet contentment in an ordinary life brings true peace.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The Latin Vulgate translates this verse as praising a poor man who provides for himself over a proud man who lacks bread.

notes.meaning: A godly person shows kindness even to animals, making sure work beasts have proper food, rest, and care. By contrast, the supposed mercy of wicked people is harsh and self-serving. Compassion toward helpless creatures reflects the heart of God.

Working hard at an honest job provides food and steady provision for a household. But chasing wild, worthless schemes shows a lack of good sense and leads to poverty. Faithful daily labor is God's normal way to meet our needs.

Sinful people covet the traps and plundered gains used by other evil men. But the inner root of the righteous person produces healthy, lasting fruit that blesses others. True blessing grows out of a quiet, faithful heart rather than stolen goods.

Sinners often get trapped by their own careless or lying words and face painful consequences. But righteous people, who guard what they say, are delivered out of danger. Careful speech protects us from bringing trouble onto our own heads.

A person reaps great personal good and inner satisfaction by speaking words that encourage and instruct others. In the same way, the work a person does with their hands brings an appropriate reward. God ensures that faithful words and deeds bear good fruit.

differ.view: Baptists emphasize that God rewarding human works does not mean people earn salvation by their own merit, but shows God's gracious kindness in accepting good works through Christ.

notes.meaning: A fool is completely convinced that his own choices are always right and refuses to be corrected. A truly wise person knows his understanding is limited and gladly listens to sound guidance. Being open to advice keeps us from ruin.

A foolish person lets his temper flare immediately when provoked, making his anger obvious to everyone. A sensible person stays calm and chooses to overlook an insult rather than escalate the fight. Self-control saves us from needless shame.

An honest witness speaks what is true and helps justice prevail in the community. But a dishonest person spreads lies and deceives others to serve wicked ends. Speaking the plain truth honors God and protects our neighbors.

Careless, sharp words can cut like a sword, wounding feelings and breaking friendships. On the other hand, the gentle and thoughtful words of the wise bring emotional healing and restore peace. We should use our tongues to mend rather than to hurt.

Words that are true stand the test of time because truth has a lasting foundation. A lie may seem clever for a moment, but it is quickly exposed and disgraced. Choosing honesty gives us a reputation that never has to fear being found out.

People who plot harm against others have deceit brewing inside their hearts and end up hurting themselves. But those who actively work to make peace and seek the good of others experience genuine joy. Promoting harmony brings deep inner happiness.

God promises that no lasting evil will ruin the righteous, because He turns even difficult trials for their ultimate good. In contrast, wicked people are overwhelmed by the misery their own sins produce. Trusting God assures us that our troubles will not have the final say.

differ.view: Baptists emphasize that no punishment for sin will ever fall on the righteous, because Christ bore all their punishment in their place.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The Latin Vulgate translation reads that nothing that happens will make the righteous person sad.

notes.meaning: The Lord detests deceitful words and lying lips because they break trust and tear society apart. He takes great delight in people who keep their promises and act with integrity. Living truthfully reflects God's own faithful character.

A prudent person does not show off what he knows, choosing instead to speak only when it truly helps others. But a fool cannot help blabbering, putting his ignorance and empty thoughts on display for all to see. Quiet modesty is a true mark of understanding.

Hard-working people earn respect, independence, and leadership over time because of their steady effort. But people who are lazy or dishonest end up in servitude and dependent on others. Consistent diligence opens the door to greater usefulness.

Worry and heavy sadness weigh down a person's heart and drain their strength. But a timely, kind word of encouragement or God's comforting promises can lift that burden and bring joy. A gentle word can renew someone's hope when they are struggling.

A godly person is careful about who he chooses as close friends, knowing that companions shape life's direction. But the path of evil people deceives them, leading them and others astray into ruin. Choosing wise companions guards our walk with God.

differ.view: Baptists emphasize that the righteous person is more excellent than his neighbor because he has been clothed in the perfect righteousness of Christ.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The Latin Vulgate translates this verse to say that a person is just if he willingly accepts a loss for the sake of a friend.

notes.meaning: A lazy person does not finish what he begins, failing even to prepare and enjoy what he hunted. In contrast, a diligent person values and uses whatever he gains through honest work. Diligence allows us to enjoy the full blessing of our labor.

Walking in the way of righteousness leads to true life and peace both now and forever. In that holy path, death has no lasting power, while turning to sinful shortcuts leads to destruction. Following God's path leads to eternal safety.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The Latin Vulgate translates the second line to say that a devious path or byway leads to death.
